outcome.technical: compose_phase_brief in plugins/audit/scripts/status/audit-lookup.py now computes each owed task's own diff once (_task_commit_diff_lines: git diff <commit>^..<commit> -- <task files> ':(exclude)docs/audit', or the empty tree for a root commit), embedded in the brief in place of the old 'diff: git show <sha> -- <files>' instruction line; added a 'Phase diff scope' section (_phase_diff_paths/_phase_scope_lines) listing the whole phase diff's changed paths and, named as such, every path outside every task's declared files; a re-review (any task for which _filed_returns.is_fix_task holds) now shows only the fix task(s)' sections under a new 'Re-review scope' note, leaving the mechanically-computed 'owed' set (still read off every task) unaffected. agents/audit-reviewer.md's 'git show <sha> -- <files> is its diff' instruction is replaced by 'each with its diff already computed in, not re-derived' plus a re-review note, trimmed to stay at 6992 bytes under tools/measure-context.py's AGENT_CEILINGS['reviewer']=7000 (verified via python3 tools/measure-context.py --gate --tree plugins/audit). reference/phase-signoff.md's description of what the phase brief hands the reviewer updated to mention the diff and the re-review case. The CLI's `brief --role` success message now also measures the written brief's byte size (a per-run artifact, never gated by AGENT_CEILINGS) and prints it - but on STDERR, because drive-phase.py's own `re.search(r"written: (.+)$", out.strip())` parses stdout alone to find the brief path; putting the size on stdout broke that parse (test_drive_phase.py fell to 166/231) until this attempt caught and fixed it, now locked by test bf1a. Tests added in plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_lookup.py: bf50 (two tasks' own commits, each touching only its own file - their per-task diffs concatenate to exactly `git diff <base> <head> -- ':(exclude)docs/audit'` over the tasks' files), bf51 (a task commit also touching a file no task declares names it under 'Paths outside every task's declared files', not the declared ones), bf52 (a phase carrying a finding whose fixTask is P1.4 lists only that task's section, not the three an earlier round already reviewed), bf1a (regression lock: stdout's 'written: <path>' line stays the path alone, with any byte count on stderr instead). python3 plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_lookup.py --selftest: 90/90 cases passed. Full sweep python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py: 331/331 files ok, 152 migrated to tests/, 15869 cases (exit 0, re-run clean after an earlier contested run on a shared, multi-agent machine showed two unrelated transient failures in test_drive_phase.py and test_stamp_verification.py that both files' own --selftest later confirmed were not real - test_drive_phase.py: 237/237, test_stamp_verification.py: 266/266 - caused by CPU contention from concurrent sibling sweeps, not by this change).
outcome.descriptive: Phase briefs now carry each owed task's own diff and the phase's whole changed-path scope computed once, so the reviewer reads rather than re-derives it, and a re-review shows only the fix tasks.

redFirst.basis: `python3 plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_lookup.py --selftest` in a throwaway tree at HEAD exited 1 with 4 of 90 collected tests failing an assertion, the task's own among them (HEAD's own tests green on HEAD's code), each passing with the working tree's implementation - bf1a (house FAIL), bf50 (house FAIL), bf51 (house FAIL), bf52 (house FAIL): SELFTEST FAILED: 86/90 cases passed; run without CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR; dependencies linked from the project root, entry by entry as symlinks: node_modules - .cache, .vite, .vite-temp are not linked and a new entry a runner makes beside the links stays in the throwaway, but a write into a linked entry lands in the project's own node_modules and is not watched; the user's .npmrc in the home directory dropped (every run has a fresh home)
